checks.source_as_cited: Clark-Wilson 1987; Biba 1977; Anderson 1972; Krohn et al. 2007 (Flume)
checks.note: All four exist as cited (Flume verified via dblp/SOSP record: Krohn, Yip, Brodsky, Cliffer, Kaashoek, Kohler, Morris, SOSP 2007 pp. 321-334; others from standard bibliographic knowledge). Mapping of CDI/UDI/IVP/TP, C4, C5 and separation of duty to the design is a faithful use of Clark-Wilson. Overreach: Clark-Wilson assumes certification of TPs and IVPs by a trusted security officer, so the 'agents not trusted to be right' are only defensible if the TPs (scripts) are themselves the trusted, certified part. Biba's low-water-mark and Flume's taint are about information flow and do not settle by themselves where taint 'should' travel; Flume additionally assumes no superuser-level bugs and leaves some covert channels. Clark-Wilson was designed for commercial data integrity (fraud and error by authorised users), not for adversarial text inputs; the analogy is reasonable but is an analogy.
checks.correction: Say the structure holds only if TPs and IVPs are deterministic, certified code outside the agents' reach, and note Flume's assumptions.

checks.source_as_cited: Clark and Wilson 1987, IEEE S&P
checks.note: Paper exists (IEEE S&P 1987, pp. 184-194). Rule C5 (a TP taking a UDI must validate or reject it, yielding a CDI) and the IVP/TP/CDI structure are as described. Assumptions about certification, enforcement (E1/E2) and logging (C4) match. From standard bibliographic knowledge and textbook descriptions, not from a fetched page.

checks.source_as_cited: Hardy 1988, The Confused Deputy, ACM SIGOPS OSR
checks.note: Real paper (OSR 22(4), Oct 1988). It argues that ambient authority (the compiler's billing-file rights) makes the deputy confusable and that capabilities, which bundle designation with authority, avoid it. Claim matches. Source: standard bibliographic knowledge.

checks.source_as_cited: Saltzer and Schroeder 1975, Proc. IEEE
checks.note: Real (Proc. IEEE 63(9), 1278-1308). Least privilege, fail-safe defaults, complete mediation, economy of mechanism and separation of privilege are all among its eight principles. The 'bounded damage' claim is the stated rationale of least privilege. Source: standard knowledge.

checks.source_as_cited: Provos, Friedl, Honeyman 2003, 'Preventing Privilege Escalation', USENIX Security
checks.note: Verified on the USENIX proceedings page: 12th USENIX Security Symposium, Aug 2003, pp. 231-242, authors as cited. Privilege separation, implemented in OpenSSH, with a small privileged monitor and unprivileged child; it blocks known OpenSSH vulnerabilities. The interface is a monitor protocol, not literally 'typed', but narrow-and-validated is the paper's point.

checks.source_as_cited: Greshake et al. 2023, AISec; Debenedetti et al. 2025, 'Defeating Prompt Injections by Design' (arXiv)
checks.note: Greshake et al. (AISec 2023, 'Not what you've signed up for...') is real and is the standard source for indirect prompt injection. CaMeL paper verified via arXiv:2503.18813 (March 2025), authors Debenedetti, Shumailov, Fan, Hayes, Carlini, Fabian, Kern, Shi, Terzis, Tramer (one aggregator lists Terzis first, so order varies by source). CaMeL uses a privileged LLM that sees only the trusted query and a quarantined LLM that reads untrusted data, with capabilities and a custom interpreter enforcing policies. 'Provable security' is claimed only on AgentDojo (67% of tasks in v1, 77% in a later version, at a utility cost), and the paper itself acknowledges side channels and the need for user-written policies. So the guarantee is strong but not unconditional.
checks.correction: Add that CaMeL's guarantee depends on correct policies and excludes side channels, and costs utility.

checks.source_as_cited: Denning 1976, 'A Lattice Model of Secure Information Flow', CACM
checks.note: Real (CACM 19(5), 236-243). Labels form a lattice, flow is allowed only upward, output label is the join of input labels; implicit flows are treated. Application to integrity is the standard dual (meet). Source: standard knowledge.

checks.source_as_cited: Myers and Liskov 1997, 'A Decentralized Model for Information Flow Control', SOSP
checks.note: Real (SOSP 1997, pp. 129-142). The model has owners, readers and declassification by an authorised principal. Declassification is the main explicit mechanism; endorsement is its integrity dual, which was developed in later work (e.g. Myers/Liskov 2000 TOSEM, Zdancewic) rather than prominently in the 1997 paper, so the 'endorsement' wording is slightly loose. Source: standard knowledge.

checks.source_as_cited: Krohn et al. 2007, Flume, SOSP
checks.note: Verified via dblp and paper excerpts: process-granularity DIFC for stock OSes (Linux, OpenBSD), run as a user-level reference monitor. Assumes no superuser-gaining bugs and closes only known covert storage channels, so 'whatever it does internally' holds for explicit flows but not all covert channels.

checks.source_as_cited: Anderson 1972, Computer Security Technology Planning Study, ESD-TR-73-51
checks.note: Real (USAF ESD-TR-73-51, Oct 1972, two volumes). It introduced the reference monitor concept with the three properties (tamper-proof, always invoked, small enough to be analysed). Source: standard knowledge and textbooks.

checks.source_as_cited: Saltzer and Schroeder 1975
checks.note: Economy of mechanism and complete mediation are two of the eight principles; the rationale is that a small, simple design is easier to inspect. Source: standard knowledge.

checks.source_as_cited: Bishop and Dilger 1996, 'Checking for Race Conditions in File Accesses', Computing Systems
checks.note: Verified via the USENIX PDF and UC Davis record: Computing Systems 9(2), Spring 1996, pp. 131-152. The paper is about detecting TOCTTOU binding flaws, with a semantic detection method and examples (xterm logging, passwd). It does not itself claim that binding the check to an immutable identifier closes the race; that remedy (operate on the object, e.g. via file descriptor, or here a content hash) is a standard consequence but is the design's inference, not the paper's guarantee.
checks.correction: Cite Bishop and Dilger for the problem and detection; present the hash-binding as the design's own mitigation.

checks.source_as_cited: Clark and Wilson 1987; Saltzer and Schroeder 1975
checks.note: Separation of duty is a Clark-Wilson requirement (rule E4/C-rules on certifier not being executor) and separation of privilege is one of Saltzer-Schroeder's principles; both state that two independent parties are needed. The no-collusion assumption is noted in both traditions. Source: standard knowledge.

checks.source_as_cited: Avizienis 1985, 'The N-Version Approach to Fault-Tolerant Software', IEEE TSE
checks.note: Real (IEEE TSE SE-11(12), 1491-1501). Independently developed versions plus a voting decision mask design faults, under an independence assumption. Source: standard knowledge.

checks.source_as_cited: Knight and Leveson 1986, IEEE TSE
checks.note: Real (IEEE TSE SE-12(1), 96-109). 27 independently written versions were run on a million inputs; the independence hypothesis was rejected at a high significance level, since versions failed together on certain inputs. Claim matches. A search result also noted that Knight et al. found problems with fault-seeding assumptions, which is a separate paper. Source: standard knowledge.

checks.source_as_cited: Biba 1977, MITRE MTR-3153
checks.note: Real (Biba, Integrity Considerations for Secure Computer Systems, MITRE MTR-3153, 1977). It defines strict integrity (no read down, no write up) and the low-water-mark policy, where a subject's level drops to that of what it reads. The 'never contaminated' guarantee applies to strict integrity with trusted labels; the low-water-mark policy keeps objects clean by degrading the subject, not by preventing contamination of the subject. Wording blends the two.
checks.correction: Distinguish strict integrity (prevents) from low-water-mark (the subject's level falls).

checks.source_as_cited: Clark and Wilson 1987
checks.note: Rule C4 requires every TP to append to a log CDI and C5 requires validation of untrusted input; the logging is done by the TP (the mechanism), not the user. The 'subject cannot forge' assumption is consistent with the model's enforcement rules. Source: standard knowledge.

checks.source_as_cited: Anderson 1972
checks.note: Tamper-proofness is a core reference-monitor requirement; the assumption that the monitor and its policy are outside the subject's write reach is the definition. Source: standard knowledge.

checks.source_as_cited: Kim and Spafford 1994, Tripwire, ACM CCS
checks.note: Real (2nd ACM CCS, Fairfax VA, Nov 1994, pp. 18-29). Tripwire stores cryptographic hashes of files and detects changes, and the paper requires the database to be kept read-only or off-host. Source: standard knowledge.

checks.source_as_cited: Biba 1977; Provos, Friedl, Honeyman 2003
checks.note: Biba no-read-down and privilege separation (verified for Provos et al.) together support the claim that a privileged part receives only validated messages. Note that 'no read down' for the most privileged subject is the design's application of Biba, not a statement in either source.

checks.source_as_cited: Saltzer and Schroeder 1975; Provos et al. 2003
checks.note: Both exist and support least privilege and a narrow interface. The claim that a steered verifier can only emit one of a fixed set of verdicts follows only if the interface really restricts output; neither source addresses an LLM verifier or the cross-check by deterministic checks, so this is design reasoning, not a cited guarantee.

checks.source_as_cited: Schneier and Kelsey 1999, 'Secure Audit Logs to Support Computer Forensics', ACM TISSEC
checks.note: Real (ACM TISSEC 2(2), May 1999, 159-176; earlier USENIX Security 1998). It uses hash chaining and per-entry keys that evolve, to give forward integrity: an attacker who compromises the logging machine at time t cannot undetectably alter entries before t. It still assumes the machine is not compromised before logging, and a trusted verifier. So 'party the subject does not control' is stronger than the paper's assumption, which tolerates later compromise of the log host. Source: standard knowledge.
checks.correction: State forward-integrity: only entries made before the compromise are protected; entries after a compromise are not.

checks.source_as_cited: Clark and Wilson 1987 (C4)
checks.note: C4 (append-only log of all TP executions) matches the claimed accountability role; reconstructibility is the stated purpose. Source: standard knowledge.

checks.source_as_cited: Clark and Wilson 1987; Kim and Spafford 1994
checks.note: Clark-Wilson rule C1/C2 requires IVPs to ensure CDIs are valid, and Tripwire provides hash-baseline checks. Combining them to re-validate a CDI before reuse is a sound reading; the out-of-reach baseline is Tripwire's stated assumption.

checks.source_as_cited: Kohnfelder and Garg 1999; Shostack 2014, Threat Modeling, Wiley
checks.note: Kohnfelder and Garg, 'The Threats to Our Products' (Microsoft, 1999, internal memo; the STRIDE origin) and Shostack's 2014 Wiley book are real. STRIDE is applied per DFD element and offers no completeness proof; the claim states that honestly. Source: standard knowledge; the Microsoft memo is not publicly archived at a stable record I could check, so the original is only reliably known through secondary descriptions.

checks.source_as_cited: Schneier 1999, 'Attack Trees', Dr. Dobb's Journal
checks.note: Real (Dr. Dobb's Journal 24(12), Dec 1999). AND/OR decomposition of attacker goals, with leaf values for analysis; its quality depends on goals being enumerated, as stated. Source: standard knowledge.

checks.source_as_cited: Mills 1972, 'On the Statistical Validation of Computer Programs', IBM Federal Systems Division
checks.note: The Wikipedia 'bebugging' article cites exactly this title, author and year as the origin of fault seeding. I could not retrieve the report text; the original is an internal IBM report, so the content is checked only through secondary descriptions. The method (seed faults, use the share found to estimate residual real faults) matches, and its known weak point is that seeded faults may not represent real ones, which the claim states. One unreliable page attributes it to 'E.K. Mills'; that is wrong.
checks.correction: Treat as an internal IBM report (1972), cited via secondary sources.

result.overall: Every cited source exists and the bibliographic details are right. I checked this with web searches for six of them: the CaMeL paper (arXiv:2503.18813), Provos et al., Flume, Bishop and Dilger, and the Mills seeding report. The rest I accepted from standard bibliographic knowledge, which I did not fetch pages to confirm. The weaker points are about what is claimed, not whether the source exists. (1) Bishop and Dilger is about detecting TOCTTOU flaws, not about hash binding as a fix. (2) Biba's strict integrity prevents contamination, while the low-water-mark policy lowers the subject's level instead. (3) Schneier and Kelsey give forward integrity only, so entries written after the log host is compromised are not protected. (4) CaMeL's guarantee is shown on AgentDojo, at a utility cost, and depends on correct policies and excludes side channels. (5) Clark-Wilson assumes certified TPs and IVPs, so the structural defence holds only if those are deterministic code the agents cannot change. (6) The 1997 decentralized label model is mainly about declassification, and endorsement comes from later work. (7) The Mills report is an internal IBM document that I could confirm only through secondary citations, and the Kohnfelder and Garg memo is similar.
